reviews.comment: The course was taught by 2 professors, I really enjoyed Gomer's half much more than Professor Hardins. Gomer focused more on long-term understanding, whereas Hardin focused on memorization and graded harder on the free-response questions. Gomer also provided all of his past years' exams, which were quite literally identical to his exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course taught by two professors, Gomer teaches second half. I found it hard to pay attention in lecture and thought that it was much more fast paced than the first half. Very exam heavy, but he offers extra points. Study the Be-Able To's as much as possible. He posts a lot of practice exams, but no answers, does not give them out in office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Gomer taught the second half of the class which in my opinion was the hardest part of the course. He makes it extremely doable and gives plenty of practice exams but without the answers. His exams are straight from the be able to's, so as long as you go over those you should be fine
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gomer was pretty ok. His exam questions came straight from his be able to's so as long as you do those you'll pass the class. He gave tons of practice exams but didnt give the answer key for them. I recommend going to the review sessions he host before each exam to ask him about the answers to the practice exam questions, or go to his office hours
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gomer's lectures rely on examples rather than fully explaining topics, often requiring textbook supplementation, Hardin's are better. His responses can feel dismissive, but his "be able to" guides closely match exams. Study these thoroughly, attend reviews for clarification, and you'll do fine! Practice exams are nice but lack answer keys so ask!
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: his lecture style just honestly isn't the best. dr hardin teaches the first half of the semester (first 2 exams) and his lectures made a lot more sense to me. gomer uses a lot of examples rather than actually teach what the topics are. however his exams come straight from the be able to's he provides so if you do those you should be fine
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Gomer. I had him for 492 (Therapeutical Developments) and 496 (Ethics in Biology).  Class is mandatory, but once a week. Have to read a chapter of a textbook before class, but is max 10 pages long. He truly cares about his students and wants to learn about every one of his students.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Caring--Respected

reviews.comment: Gomer was not as serious Hardin, sometimes making jokes instead of answering questions. Was a bit condescending when talking to him. Gave lots of practice exams but no answer key for them. His lectures were not as helpful, had to use textbook to supplement. Study be able tos, since that's what the exam is, and ask if confused about 1 at his review!

Gomer was paired with Hardin. Gomer's lectures were short and not as detailed, but his test was easier. Go to his review before the tests to clarify the be able to questions. He was available during office hours to answer questions but was a bit condescending. He would go over the be able to if you asked him though. he gave extra points on final
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: To be honest, his lecture style wasn't for me. And he is a little soft spoken so sit at the front of the class. His exams are super easy and fair though and they are literally from the Be Able To's. Hardin was a better lecturer but his exams were harder and more specific. I made B's on both of Hardins exams, but made 100s on Gomers.

Draw everything out. Not very detailed lecturer but his exams were straight be-able-to's. His review sessions were helpful. Could be condescending but nice and always tried to help out. Study his mock exams.

He's not the best lecturer but i'm giving him a good rating because he lets you know what to study. He won't try to trick you and his exams are literally the be able to's. I just wished he taught the entire semester because hardins exams were SIGNIFICANTLY harder.

Gomer teaches the second half of the class, and although very knowledgeable about the subject he almost breaks down the material too much where you aren't able to comprehend the complex topics. His tests are straight from the be able to's. He expects you to have read the textbook before coming to class and then only briefly explains the topics.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His exams are straight from the be able to's. Was able to study significantly less then Hardin's tests and do better. Highly recommend, he cracks a lot of jokes in class and tries to keep everyone engaged.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a little quiet but enjoyable. Very kind and though he was a really good prof I enjoyed Hardin a little more since Gomer got a little boring at times. Go to his review sessions the day before the tests. The tests are literally just the be-able-tos so super duper easy

Both Hardin and Gomer are very knowledgeable and helpful if you don't understand a concept. The only hard part about the class is the material. Just make sure you pay attention to the "be able to's" and the practice exams. Gomer especially focuses on the "be able to's" for his exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Gomer with Dr. Hardin and I overall really enjoyed the class. I find the material very interesting, but there's a lot of material and you have to work for your grade. Gomer is funny, knowledgeable, and an easy grader. I also like how he relates class material to real world medicine. Hoping for an A, but worst case I'll end up with a B.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gomer was teaching this class along with professor Hardin his tests were easier and he graded generously but this class is really lecture heavy and absolutely NO extra credit u grade is based of 4 exams and u have to study to pass he is really kind and I liked him but this class was one the hardest I ever took. It has so much material.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do NOT take him. Each class he asks to hear personal/class questions so he can give advice, seems good just don't be fooled. I reached out to him ab/ dropping the class before the final & told me that I'd do great. I failed his class by less than a point (he would not bump me). He uses it against u if u miss hwk, if you need to learn, he's not it.

Dr. Gomer is the best biology professor I have had so far. His teaching is straight forward, just like his test questions, and he goes in depth on important concepts. I never had to read the textbook, just attend lecture and read his powerpoints. He is very knowledgeable and caring. Would definitely pick Dr. Gomer as your prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Gomer with Hardin and really enjoyed the class, especially Gomer's section of it. He creates "Be able tos" for each chapter that clearly states what you need to know for each chapter, if you put in the work to really learn those sections you will ace every test. I also loved that all test questions related to real-life examples.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I hate this class. Definitely made me depressed. Gomer way of teaching is absolutely trash. He oversimplifies things in a bad way so lectures are useless. Exams are supper hard and there is absolutely no curve or anything to help your grade. just don't do it or you'll be mourning your grade. I am pretty sure I failed and I spent time prep a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the worst teacher I have ever had to deal with at TAMU so far. He was vague in his lectures and went through them with 20 minutes left of class because he doesn't explain anything. He treats/talks to us as children and thinks that TV addiction is the reason people don't come to his class, but in reality, it's him. Good Luck
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is probably the hardest course I have taken at A&M due to the sheer amount of material and its specificity, but it is doable. But I learned so much. Gomer was really passionate about teaching and coming to class was enjoyable. This class ate up most of my time, so if you're taking a lot of other hard classes, then take someone else!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Taking team taught course with Hardin/Gomer. Very challenging class. 3 exams and a final. Biweekly homework. However, if you put in the work, you will do well because the expectations are clear. I recommend reading book before class and then engaging yourself in lectures. SI and studying consistently is key.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He was pretty dope. His half was a lot easier than Hardin's. He explained the subjects less specific than Hardin though which made test's a little harder to prepare for. All I did was read the book before his class, took my notes by his "be able to's" during lecture, then wrote answers to all the "be able to's" on a blank piece of paper. Easy A
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Exam averages were terrible, no curve, and he is not clear on lectures at all. Spent too much time answering unrelated questions from others and he rushed through important material. His 'think-pair-share" activities were useless, and made me anxious. Friends and I had to drop, it was disappointing.

This has been the only class I have ever dropped at this institution. He taught this class alongside another professor who was about the same as him. Exams were TOUGH and no matter how long I studied I still made poor grades. I studied hard, and I've never felt more disappointed with any class--I would advice anyone against taking BIO 213 with him.
